    🪨 Gedarism¶

    "Stone is the bone. Coil is the muscle. Together they hold."

    Gedarism is the shared faith of Xobkua (Giants) and Zakarutia (Snake People) — two species that could not be more different in body, bound by one theology on the southern Demon Continent. Giants are 3-meter territorial builders; snakes are matriarchal, venomous, river-and-desert tacticians. Gedarism teaches that both are organs of the same body: Gedar, the World-Pillar that coils.

    The name Gedar is the Giants' word for the stone that remembers being squeezed, and the snakes' word for the squeeze that remembers stone.

    Origins¶

    Gedarism predates the snake–giant split in memory. Xobkua's island is one-quarter the size of the Demon Continent — so massive it is considered a continuation of the continent — and Zakarutia's south-coast plains face it across a narrow sea. Long before queens and clan longhouses, both peoples told the same story when they met to trade: a great pillar held the Demon Continent up while a great serpent coiled it so it would not wander.

    By Age 6, the story had formalized into a dual priesthood:

    • Giant Stone-Singers — clan elders who vibrate longhouse beams with deep-toned chanting until the wood hums. They claim the tone proves Gedar's bone is still load-bearing.
    • Snake Coil-Mothers — Zakarutian matriarchs who perform the coil-dance, wrapping and unwrapping dyed silk around a central basalt pillar to show how pressure creates strength.

    The faith has no single founder. Its "prophet" is the Strait itself — the sea between Xobkua and Zakarutia, which both peoples pilgrimage to drink from (Giants wading, snakes undulating) on the same tide-day each year.

    Beliefs¶

    • Gedar is pillar and coil at once — not two gods, but one god seen from two ends. Giants emphasize the pillar (endurance, holding, architectural truth). Snakes emphasize the coil (pressure, patience, constriction). Orthodoxy insists neither is complete alone; heresy is choosing one half.
    • The world is held, not made — unlike creation faiths (Maomism, Dwarvism), Gedarism does not claim Gedar made Ge'or. It claims Gedar keeps it from drifting — a maintenance theology. Neglect, not rebellion, is the sin.
    • Territory is trust — Giant territoriality (defending Xobkua fiercely, seeking no conquest) and Zakarutian matriarchal patience (the old Queen endlessly rebuilding her archaic fleet to retake lost Xikxia) are both taught as Gedarist virtues: hold what is yours with absolute fidelity; do not grasp what is not.
    • Sibbism alongside, not against — Zakarutia's majority faith is Sibbism (Snake Goddess + 24 demigod sons at the world's corners). Gedarism does not replace Sibbism; it undergirds it. In Zakarutian theology, the Snake Goddess is Gedar seen from the coil-side; in Xobkuan shrugs, "your goddess is our pillar's wife, that is fine." The tie is diplomatic as much as doctrinal — it is why Xobkua trades with Zakarutia when all others keep their distance, and why Asatru respects both from across the sea.
    • No conquest, no conversion — Gedarism has no missionary impulse. A Giant clan longhouse and a Zakarutian matriarch's court are both complete Gedarist worship without needing to agree on detail. The Strait pilgrimage is the only required observance, and even it may be performed by proxy.

    Practices¶

    • Strait Pilgrimage (The Holding Day) — on the first spring tide after Maenar's dark phase, delegations from both nations wade/drink at the narrow water. Giants carry a quarried stone; snakes carry a silk coil; they exchange them at mid-strait and carry the other's token home. To drop the token before reaching shore is a grave omen.
    • Stone-Singing — Giant longhouses (30–50 Giants, timber beams weighing tons) are blessed by singing until the frame resonates. A longhouse that sings cleanly is Gedar-approved; one that rattles must be rebuilt.
    • Coil-Dance and Fleet-Blessing — before the Zakarutian fleet sails (the Queen's long-prepared reconquest of Xikxia, lost 589 AGD), Coil-Mothers dance the coil around the basalt pillar in the palace. The fleet's archaism is itself a Gedarist point: patient pressure over flash.
    • Silence of the Pillar — doctrinal disputes are resolved by a day of shared silence between a Giant Stone-Singer and a Snake Coil-Mother, sitting on opposite sides of the Strait. Whichever speaks first has conceded impatience, not error; the matter is tabled for a year.
    • Oral memory — Giants keep Gedarist history in sung tones that vibrate through the ground; snakes keep it in heat-shimmer ancestor veneration (dead queens watched in desert shimmer). Both agree the form of memory does not matter — only that it is held.

    Influence¶

    • Majority (syncretic): Xobkua — universal among Giants (often the only faith); Zakarutia — majority Sibbism but Gedarism is the official state tie (the Queen's court observes both; the fleet is blessed in both)
    • Diplomatic hinge: the Strait Pilgrimage is the sole regular diplomatic contact between Xobkua and the mainland, and the reason Zakarutia enjoys Giant timber/stone for fleet repair despite its isolation
    • Asatru view: the Asatru Empire officially respects Gedarism without endorsing it — a "southern maintenance faith" that, usefully, keeps two potentially disruptive southern powers loyal to each other's calendar rather than to mainland adventurism
    • Yaoma Tribe neighbors note Gedarism with maritime amusement: "they hold the world so it does not wander; we sail the part they forgot to hold still"
